extracted.intended_audience: researchers (especially early-career) and academics interested in learning to perform peer review
extracted.subtask_description: A short modular training/course aimed at teaching researchers how to perform high-quality peer reviews: deciding whether to accept requests, writing the review report, understanding journal/editor requirements and peer-review models, and post-review actions. Leads to a certificate on completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding whether to accept a review request
rubrics_metrics.description: What to consider before deciding to accept a request or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page states learners will learn 'what to consider before deciding to accept a request or not' as part of the course; no further specifics are listed on the page (but implies consideration of suitability, capacity, and potential conflicts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formulating the review report
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course promises instruction on 'how to formulate your report' — i.e., structuring and writing a peer review — though the post does not list the report structure or checklist items explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking journal- and editor-specific requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: How to check journal- and editor requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learners are taught to verify and follow specific instructions from journals and editors when preparing a review, ensuring the review meets editorial policies and submission formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding different peer review models
rubrics_metrics.description: How the different peer review models operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course covers the operation of different peer review models (e.g., the page phrase: 'how the different peer review models operate'). The post does not enumerate them, but emphasizes knowledge of model differences as an evaluative/operational criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions and responsibilities after submitting a review
rubrics_metrics.description: What you can do after completing your report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction includes post-review steps and responsibilities ('what you can do after completing your report'), such as follow-up communication or responding to editor queries (not detailed on the page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing vital ground skills and reviewer competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Gaining vital ground skills and improving competence in peer reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course is described as helping potential referees 'to develop by gaining vital ground skills and improving their competence in peer reviewing.' Course features supporting this include expert-developed syllabus, modular material, mixed formats, and question checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence and readiness to accept review invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Building confidence to accept invites and 'remove the fear factor' associated with peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course aims to make learners 'confident and active referees' and 'enable a new generation of referees to help confidently shape the research output' so they will be willing to say 'yes' to invites. Certification is advertised as a public signal of referee expertise to editors and (possibly) institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing understanding and receiving community feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Using module questions to test understanding and obtaining feedback via a community (Mendeley group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material is 'organized in a modular format with questions accompanying each section, allowing you to test your understanding and work at your own pace.' Learners can 'raise questions and obtain feedback in the associated Mendeley group.' A certificate is awarded on completion of the full course.
